plan.title: Maya answers everything in her first text (page example)

transcript.text: hi! I'm Maya, I want to read about stoicism every morning at home before work, maybe 10 min

Hi Maya, I'm ZOH! I'll help you get better at one thing, with a small step each day. Stoicism every morning is a great pick. You can text "stop" anytime, and you can change how I coach just by telling me, like "chill out" or "push me harder."

What time do you want to read each morning? A set time makes it stick, so pick something like 7:00 or 7:30.
Around 7:45, at home before work. I've got about 10 minutes then. I have a paperback of Meditations already, and I read some Marcus Aurelius in college but nothing since.

Love that you already own the paperback and have some Marcus in your past. Where do you want this to get you? It could be finishing Meditations, or having a few ideas you can actually use. "Not sure yet" works too.

Honestly I just want to read and learn more about stoic philosophy every morning. Finishing Meditations would be nice but not a must, I'm more into actually understanding the ideas and maybe using some of them.

Wanting to understand and use the ideas, not just finish the book, is a great way to read Marcus. Here's the plan:

• Where it's headed: understand stoic ideas and use a few in daily life
• Day 1 (today, since 7:45 has passed): tonight at 8:00 pm at home, read Book 2 of Meditations for 10 min. Pick one line that stands out.
• Usual schedule: every day at 7:45 am, at home, 10 min. I'll text you a heads-up at 7:35.
• Proof: a 30-second voice note saying that line in your own words and where you could use it. Alternative: a photo of the page with the line marked.
• Why: putting ideas in your own words is what makes them stick.

Each day's step builds on how the last one went, toward actually using the ideas, not just reading them. What do you think?

grade.summary: ZOH covered the key onboarding inputs in three texts and gave Maya a clear, specific plan built on her reading goal, time and paperback. The main weak spots are a fairly mild energy level for the Pushy default and a heads-up reminder promise the app may not send.
